_about: The mathematics problem book's registry: key books and named classics. See principles/problem-books.md. Every named classic here is solved in a problem set; "where" points to it.
intro: Each of these problems turns on one idea: a bijection, an invariant, a symmetry, a clever bound. Look for the idea before you calculate.
lede: Climb the ladder from Level 1, or pick a set; look for the idea before you calculate, and open a hint only when you're stuck.

stage.title: By topic
stage.blurb: Three sets of classic results, each with hints and full proofs, from warm-ups to problems that need a real idea.

books.title: Proofs from THE BOOK
books.author: Martin Aigner & Günter M. Ziegler
books.when: The most beautiful known proofs of classic theorems. Read a chapter after each set here, to see the same results proved even more elegantly.

books.title: Problem-Solving Strategies
books.author: Arthur Engel
books.when: Olympiad problems organised by technique: invariants, pigeonhole, extremal principle, induction. After P1.

books.title: How to Solve It
books.author: George Pólya
books.when: The classic short book on how to attack a problem you can't yet see how to start. Before anything else.

books.title: The Art and Craft of Problem Solving
books.author: Paul Zeitz
books.when: Strategy and tactics with hundreds of problems, warmly written. Alongside all three sets.

books.title: Problems and Theorems in Analysis
books.author: George Pólya & Gábor Szegő
books.when: The great classic collection of analysis problems, with solutions. After P2, for the boss problems.

books.title: Mathematical Puzzles: A Connoisseur's Collection
books.author: Peter Winkler
books.when: Puzzles like the hundred prisoners, with ingenious solutions. After P3.

books.title: Book of Proof
books.author: Richard Hammack
books.when: A free, friendly introduction to writing proofs: logic, induction, contradiction, sets and functions. If proofs are new to you, read it first.

hard.title: Fermat's little theorem by necklaces
hard.idea: Non-constant strings of p beads fall into rotation classes of exactly p, so p divides aᵖ − a.
hard.visual: The strings of three beads in two colours, grouped by rotation.

hard.title: The primes are not too sparse
hard.idea: If Σ1/p converged, too few numbers up to N could be built from primes at all. Erdős's counting proof fits on a napkin.
hard.visual: Σ1/p against ln ln x: slow divergence.

hard.title: Every Pythagorean triple
hard.idea: Lines of rational slope through (−1, 0) hit the unit circle at every rational point, giving (m² − n², 2mn, m² + n²).
hard.visual: The circle with rational lines fanning out from (−1, 0).

hard.title: Catalan numbers by reflection
hard.idea: Reflect a bad path after its first touch of y = x + 1: bad paths match all paths to (n − 1, n + 1).
hard.visual: A path and its reflected tail.

hard.title: Erdős–Szekeres
hard.idea: Label each term by its longest increasing and decreasing runs; n² + 1 labels can't all fit in an n × n grid.
hard.visual: A sequence with its labels plotted as grid points.

hard.title: The Basel problem
hard.idea: 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + … = π²/6, squeezed between two sums of cot² that de Moivre's formula computes exactly.
hard.visual: Partial sums closing in on π²/6 between the two bounds.

hard.title: Stirling's formula
hard.idea: n!e^n/n^(n+½) decreases to a positive limit; Wallis's product pins it at √(2π).
hard.visual: The ratio n!/Stirling against n, approaching 1 like e^(1/12n).

hard.title: Gibbs's overshoot
hard.idea: Fourier partial sums overshoot a jump by 9% however many terms you take: the peak tends to (2/π)Si(π) = 1.179.
hard.visual: Partial sums of the square wave with a slider for N (interactive).

hard.title: Buffon's needle
hard.idea: Expected crossings are proportional to length for any shape of wire; a circle always crosses twice, so P = 2ℓ/πd.
hard.visual: Needles on a lined floor and the running estimate of π.

hard.title: Triangles on a sphere
hard.idea: Three pairs of lunes cover the sphere once and the triangle three times: area = R²(α + β + γ − π).
hard.visual: A spherical triangle with its three lunes shaded.

hard.title: Colouring a cube
hard.idea: Burnside: average the colourings each rotation fixes. With three colours, 57 cubes.
hard.visual: The ten two-coloured cubes, and the rotation types with their face cycles.

hard.title: The fifteen puzzle
hard.idea: Permutation parity plus the blank's distance parity never changes, so Loyd's 14–15 swap is unreachable.
hard.visual: The puzzle with each move flipping both parities.

hard.title: A hundred prisoners
hard.idea: Follow the cycles: everyone is freed exactly when the permutation has no cycle longer than 50, probability 31%.
hard.visual: A random permutation's cycles, and success probability against n approaching 1 − ln 2.
